thread:
anika: quick follow-up from the Quota Interface consolidation RFC — trying to capture the migration plan + open tradeoffs.
julian: thanks! can you list the compatibility guarantees again? we need to sign off for Dedicated customers.
maya: summary we discussed on the call: preserve per-tenant token semantics, keep a short-lived shim for LeaseAPI, and provide an opt-in strict-mode for new ledger semantics.
liam: +1. main risk is double-counting during the migration window if clients hit both old and new paths.
anika: exactly. proposed mitigation: a 2-week gradual rollout where the shim emits a mapping header and the runtime can dedupe by request-id. example shim header: X-Quota-Shim: ledger-v1=>ledger-v2;shim-id=anika-1
julian: can you show the dedupe logic? a tiny pseudocode snippet would help ops.
anika: sure — pseudocode:
```
if request.headers["X-Quota-Map"]:
  if seen(request.id): return ACCEPTED_WITHOUT_CHARGE
  else: mark_seen(request.id); forward_to_ledger()
else:
  forward_to_legacy()
```
liam: works, but how do we handle partial failures where legacy returns success and ledger times out?
maya: plan is to make legacy authoritative during the migration windows. ledger writes are best-effort then reconciled asynchronously. reconciliation job will surface mismatch alerts.
julian: reconciliation cadence? and SLO for it?
anika: daily reconciliation job initially; target: surface >0.1% mismatch as P1 for 24h. long-term we want continuous streaming reconciler but not in week 1.
liam: what about abuse signals — clients that rapidly switch between endpoints to bypass throttles?
anika: good call. we add a cross-path abuse detector in the ingress that tracks client fingerprint + sketch counter across both APIs. detection rules: >3x baseline QPS while burst credits disabled -> soft-block and alert.
maya: do we have telemetry fields in the new ledger for that? need a per-request abuse_score tag.
anika: yes — ledger will return abuse_score:[0-100] in its response metadata. ingress will use score>60 to route to probation pool.
julian: does that require SDK changes? we should avoid SDK churn for minor telemetry.
anika: SDKs optional. the ledger exposes the header X-Quota-Abuse: 72 and Console will show a per-customer trend. SDKs can surface but not required.
liam: ops-bot — can you schedule a canary for the shim rollout in prod-stable-noncritical cluster next Tuesday?
ops-bot: scheduled canary: prod-stable-noncritical on 2024-11-12T08:30Z. watchers: @eng-infra, @oncall. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: canary started on prod-stable-noncritical @ 2024-11-12T08:30Z — build r2024.11.12-shim. logs: https://deploys/redwood/canary/1739990000
maya: for telemetry — add these fields to the quota events: ledger_version, shim_id, request_id, abuse_score, reconciled:boolean.
anika: agreed. also adding a metric for dedupe_rate to measure how often requests hit both paths.
julian: final ask from me: public-facing SLA note for Dedicated customers — will there be a breaking window?
anika: no breaking changes. we will deprecate LeaseAPI 90 days after 100% ledger adoption per tenant, with email + console banner + automated migration assist.
liam: sounds safe. can we include an emergency rollback plan if reconciliation shows >1% undercharging?
anika: yes — rollback toggles: shim.pass_through=true (back to legacy-only) and pause-ledger-ingest flag. documented in the playbook.
maya: I'll add the playbook steps and a runbook snippet for oncall.
anika: thanks all — I'll update the RFC with the migration timeline, headers, and reconciler SLOs. ping here when the canary runs so we can watch dedupe_rate and abuse_score drift. :eyes:
julian: thx, talk later.
__notes: Single-thread Slack export. Messages are chronological, short, with code samples and bot messages. No title field per agents.md.
